analysis.title: GS Malmstrom - Few charts to end the week
key_insights: Momentum factor in the US has given back all of its gains for 2026, and Cyclicals vs Defensives has followed a similar pattern.
GS prime brokerage data showed the 5th largest hedge fund de-grossing event this year on Thursday, driven by long selling.
Hedge fund gross exposure remains elevated while net leverage continues to come down.
Cost of capital keeps rising, and the capex super-cycle is increasing competition for capital at a time of higher interest rates.
Tech is no longer capital-light. US hyperscalers' operating cash flow is becoming insufficient to fund capex, which raises their reliance on external financing.
Hyperscaler leverage remains low compared to the broader market, and the same holds for the European Tech sector.
Other things equal, a 100bp increase in the cost of debt would reduce SXXP earnings by 3%.
In Europe, interest expense as a % of sales is rising and Net Debt to EBITDA has started to pick up.
3Q earnings surprises have been slightly below the historical average.
Analysts expect 24% EPS growth going into H2, or 15% excluding commodities.
earnings_insights: 3Q earnings surprises have been slightly below the historical average (estimate-vs-reported basis not specified in the report).
Analysts expect 24% EPS growth going into H2 (consensus forecast), and 15% excluding commodities.

macro_indicators.reading: 100bp increase in cost of debt reduces SXXP earnings by 3%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher borrowing costs are a direct earnings headwind for European equities, other things equal.
Consensus growth is heavily supported by commodities. The underlying ex-commodities rate is about 9 points lower.

risk_factors: Rising cost of capital and higher interest rates.
The capex super-cycle is intensifying competition for capital.
US hyperscaler operating cash flow is insufficient to fund capex, increasing reliance on external financing.
Rising interest burden in Europe, with interest expense as a % of sales and Net Debt to EBITDA both increasing.
Continued weakness in the momentum factor and further hedge fund de-grossing.
